criteria.ABSTAIN:
Refuse to act: no offered operation can be chosen with enough confidence, and a
wrong click, select, or submission would be worse than stopping. This is not BLOCKED - BLOCKED
means no supported operation can progress, while ABSTAIN means progress exists but none of it is
trustworthy right now. A person should review the page.
criteria.CLICK: Click an element, button, menu option, autocomplete suggestion, or calendar day.
criteria.REOBSERVE:
Look at the page again before deciding. Choose this when the page is still
changing, an expected control has not appeared yet, or the evidence for every offered action is
unclear. Re-observing is cheap and is always better than acting on a stale or half-read page.
criteria.TYPE_TEXT: Enter or replace text in an editable field. A small LLM will supply the value from the goal.
criteria.WAIT: Wait for the page to update

page.text:
Question
5
of
5
How long should answers be?
Here is the same answer three ways. You can change this in Settings.
Brief
Balanced
Detailed
Why does spaced repetition work?
Each review that lands just as you start to forget takes effort to recall, and that effort strengthens the memory. Spacing reviews over days gets the same result as cramming with fewer, shorter sessions.
Canvases are saved in this browser on this device. Clearing site data removes them, so export important ones.

Here is the same answer three ways. You can change this in Settings.
Brief
Balanced
Detailed
Why does spaced repetition work?
Each review that lands just as you start to forget takes effort to recall, and that effort strengthens the memory. Spacing reviews over days gets the same result as cramming with fewer, shorter sessions.

Each review that lands just as you start to forget takes effort to recall, and that effort strengthens the memory. Spacing reviews over days gets the same result as cramming with fewer, shorter sessions.

Classes & Objects in Java
OOP Java Tutorial — Page 1 of 3
What is a Class?
A class is a blueprint for creating objects. It defines the properties (fields) and behaviours (methods) that every object
of that type will have. Think of a class like a cookie-cutter — the class defines the shape, and each object is a cookie
made from it.
public class Student
{
private String
name;
private int
grade;
public Student(String
name,
int
grade)
{
this.name
=
name;
this.grade
=
grade;
}
public String
getName()
{
return
name;
}
public void
setName(String
n)
{
name
=
n;
}
}
Creating Objects
Objects are created with the new keyword, which calls the class constructor to initialise the new instance. Each object
gets its own copy of instance variables on the heap.
Student alice
=
new
Student("Alice",
95);
System.out.println(alice.getName());
//
"Alice"
Encapsulation
Encapsulation hides internal state and requires all interaction to go through public methods. Mark fields as private and
expose them through getters and setters. This prevents invalid data and lets you add validation later without changing
the public API.

Classes & Objects in Java
OOP Java Tutorial — Page 1 of 3
What is a Class?
A class is a blueprint for creating objects. It defines the properties (fields) and behaviours (methods) that every object
of that type will have. Think of a class like a cookie-cutter — the class defines the shape, and each object is a cookie
made from it.
public class Student
{
private String
name;
private int
grade;
public Student(String
name,
int
grade)
{
this.name
=
name;
this.grade
=
grade;
}
public String
getName()
{
return
name;
}
public void
setName(String
n)
{
name
=
n;
}
}
Creating Objects
Objects are created with the new keyword, which calls the class constructor to initialise the new instance. Each object
gets its own copy of instance variables on the heap.
Student alice
=
new
Student("Alice",
95);
System.out.println(alice.getName());
//
"Alice"
Encapsulation
Encapsulation hides internal state and requires all interaction to go through public methods. Mark fields as private and
expose them through getters and setters. This prevents invalid data and lets you add validation later without changing
the public API.
